reason: The cited evidence strongly supports grain refinement, supersaturated solid solution, and hardness increase from carbon addition, but provides no direct evidence for carbon segregation at grain boundaries or its effect on creep resistance.
premises: Carbon addition during magnetron sputtering of CrNbTaTiW films refines grain size from ~35 nm to ~10 nm
Carbon forms a supersaturated solid solution without carbide formation at ~8 at.% C
Grain refinement increases hardness significantly (from 14.7 to 19.1 GPa)
Carbon segregation at grain boundaries stabilizes the refined structure and inhibits dislocation motion
Refined, stabilized grain boundaries reduce time-dependent plastic deformation (creep)
